deviation: The draft force majeure clause has no termination right when an event continues (standard: 60 days; fallback: 90 days), and it doesn't exclude supplier staffing and subcontractor failures from force majeure. Without these, Arcadia could be stuck indefinitely with unperformed services, and Ironbridge could excuse itself for its own staffing or subcontractor problems.
suggested_text: 12.5 Force Majeure. Neither Party is liable for delay caused by events beyond its reasonable control, provided it notifies the other promptly and uses reasonable efforts to resume performance. Supplier staffing shortages, labor disputes limited to Ironbridge's workforce, and failures of Ironbridge's subcontractors or suppliers are not events beyond Ironbridge's reasonable control for purposes of this Section. This Section does not excuse Ironbridge's obligations to maintain reasonable business continuity measures. Either Party may terminate the affected services on written notice if the event continues for more than 60 days.
